---
title: "Assignment 1 — Crystal structures and CIF files"
---

This first laboratory connects the crystallographic language used in the course
with an actual structure file. Before the session, review the ideas of unit
cell, fractional coordinates, asymmetric unit, symmetry-equivalent positions
and space group.

You are **not** expected to write Python code. The notebooks provide the code
needed to inspect the structure. Your task is to understand what the
calculation is doing and to interpret the crystallographic information that it
returns.

## Before the laboratory

Open your existing Mineral Science Codespace and update the distributed course
material:

```bash
update-course
```

Then create your working copy of Laboratory 1:

```bash
start-lab 01
```

Open:

```text
work/lab01/
```

You should find:

```text
01-guided-mgo.ipynb
02-assigned-structure.ipynb
data/MgO.cif
```

The first notebook is completed together during the laboratory using MgO
(periclase). The second notebook is an individual activity based on a CIF
assigned by the instructor.

::: {.callout-important}
## Work only in `work/lab01/`

Do not edit the original files under `course/labs/lab01/`.
:::

## What you should be able to explain afterwards

By the end of the activity you should be able to explain:

- what information a CIF contains;
- the difference between the asymmetric unit and the complete unit cell;
- how symmetry operations generate equivalent atomic positions;
- what a Wyckoff position and its multiplicity represent;
- why a numerical symmetry search requires a tolerance;
- why visualizing a structure is useful for inspection but does not replace a
  crystallographic analysis.

Your answers are written directly in the notebooks. No separate report is
required.
